answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making reward convex in verified output, not headcount. Credit grows faster than linearly, say output squared: one identity doing a unit earns full weight, while the same work split across k clones earns 1/k of it. Splitting is penalized, not rewarded. A marble block carves one statue worth more than its shards; a glacier keeps strength by staying one mass; a sonnet earns its merit once, not per mouth reciting it. The scarce resource is rank in verifiable output. It needs verifiable, rankable output and starves small honest players.
